overview: The shared client has two layers. client-core owns the authenticated HTTP/WebSocket connection, the local workspace replica, retries, cached files and WebRTC media. ui turns that state into conversations, dialogs and controls, while a Platform adapter supplies browser or desktop storage, notifications and hosting. The client keeps responsive optimistic state but still depends on server authorization and durable storage acknowledgements. The completed N-series work fixes particular storage, close, mute, form and file-cache failures; the Q-series report records additional races that remain open.

entries.summary: Defines the public API of the client-core package.
details: Re-exports the workspace client, typed REST client, huddle session, file cache and notification rules.
Also exposes the plain-data draft, outbox and record merge functions so browser storage and Electron's main process can use the same rules.

entries.summary: Turns workspace operations into typed HTTP requests.
details: The private request helper adds the bearer token and JSON body, combines caller cancellation with optional deadlines, and translates non-success responses into ApiError with a status and code.

Methods cover authentication, profiles, channels, message history and search, reactions, schedules, app administration, audit entries and operating status. UI code calls these methods instead of constructing endpoints repeatedly.
File uploads expose progress and cancellation. File bytes use authenticated fetch; a separately scoped download ticket supports native downloads without placing the session token into a download URL.
normalizeServerUrl interprets addresses typed by a person and rejects unsupported URL shapes. This normalizer is distinct from the stricter exact-address normalization used for local-work trust.

entries.summary: Coordinates one live workspace connection and the local state the UI renders.
details: WorkspaceClient combines Api, FileCache and a Zustand store. The store holds authenticated identity, users, channels, memberships, read cursors, loaded history, drafts, pending sends, app replies, forms and huddle state.

The WebSocket hello includes the session token, protocol version and last observed event sequence. Ready snapshots and replay events rebuild the replica; reconnect delay grows up to 30 seconds. Authentication, forced-password and protocol refusals stop ordinary reconnect loops.

History requests carry identity and snapshot watermarks so late HTTP pages can be reconciled with socket events. Identical loads share work; superseded, revoked or evicted history requests are aborted. A timeline holds at most 300 messages and inactive history is bounded by a 20-entry cache limit.

send creates a random request nonce and an optimistic PendingMessage, uploads files, posts the message and reconciles the response or socket echo by nonce. The outbox accepts up to 50 waiting sends per account. A known server refusal waits for deliberate Retry; an uncertain outcome can retry the same nonce.

Restored outbox entries contain attachment descriptions rather than File objects. Missing attachment bytes and sends older than the retry window remain visibly failed instead of silently sending incomplete or stale content. destroy releases sockets, timers, media, previews and cached files.

The N05 fix binds submitModal and dismissModal to a view ID, and N10 sends retention roots to FileCache even when old thread history has been evicted. Existing choice sequencing covers pins, saves, snooze and channel preferences, but Q09 identifies an unresolved reordered Follow/Unfollow request and Q10 an older identical Mark unread failure that can roll back newer local intent.

joinHuddle loads the call code on demand, gives the session a way to re-read /api/rtc-config, sends huddle.report only to servers that advertise huddleReports (an older server closes the socket on an unknown message), and keeps the last call's log for Diagnostics after leaving.

entries.summary: Merges individual conversation drafts without replacing the whole account's draft map.
details: DraftChanges carries put, remove, optional fill and optional base values. A window writes only conversations it changed, so saving one conversation does not erase another window's unrelated draft.

When the confirmed stored text differs from the writer's base, keepBothDrafts preserves both texts; it avoids concatenation if one text already contains the other. A removal cannot erase a concurrent newer nonempty draft.
fill brings old drafts across only into empty slots. Validation and version-envelope helpers let both storage adapters interpret the same plain data.

entries.summary: Provides a shared, revisioned durable representation of queued messages.
details: Each entry is indexed by the send nonce and carries a revision. A merge accepts a newer entry, preserving newer refusal or retry intent instead of letting a stale window overwrite it.

Delivered or discarded sends leave tombstones that prevent another window from reintroducing its old copy. A compactedThrough floor continues refusing older absent entries after individual tombstones are trimmed.
The merge keeps at least 500 tombstones, additionally retaining those inside the send retry window, with a 10,000 upper bound. This bounds the record while preserving removal intent.
Stored outboxes can be read from the current version-2 shape or an earlier plain entry array. Attachment metadata survives; preview URLs and raw File objects do not.

entries.summary: Merges a small map of string choices by the names actually changed.
details: RecordChanges maps names to strings or null for removal. Updating one account's notification-preview choice leaves other accounts' choices intact.

Shape and size checks constrain incoming changes; damaged stored entries are dropped individually while valid siblings survive. This is a plain-data primitive, so caller policy decides what unreadable privacy choices mean.

entries.summary: Fetches authenticated attachments once and owns their object-URL lifetime.
details: Concurrent requests for one file share an in-flight promise. At most four transfers run at once, including the complete body transfer, and releasing the last active view cancels unfinished work.
Active views retain their files; idle files follow an LRU-style budget of 32 MiB. Object URLs are revoked when trimmed, invalidated or disposed.

Every cached or fetching file remembers its channel, message and thread root when known. N10 adds whole-root invalidation so retention removes reply images even after their original history page was evicted.

Unknown ownership is invalidated conservatively on relevant removals. A held transfer checks that it is still current before creating a URL, and onInvalidate tells an open preview to show unavailability. This removes previously cached content; server access checks still authorize new fetches.

entries.summary: Holds the call log line type and the words for why a call has not connected.
details: Kept apart from the call itself, which loads only on joining, so the huddle bar and Diagnostics can explain trouble without loading it.

entries.summary: Owns microphone capture, WebRTC peer connections and call media state.
details: HuddleSession creates a mesh connection per participant with fixed microphone, camera and screen transceivers. Deterministic offer ownership prevents both peers from offering at once; camera and screen changes use replaceTrack instead of another negotiation.

Microphone recovery asks again for the chosen microphone, falling back to the system default after loss, replaces audio tracks for peers, and exposes micLost with device-change retry when no microphone is available.

setMicrophone and setCamera change devices mid-call: the new device opens (asked for exactly) before the old one stops, so one that will not start rejects and leaves the call as it was. Once open it reaches every peer through replaceTrack on the fixed slot, with no renegotiation, keeping the mute choice. A counter per kind drops an older choice that finishes after a newer one. A camera that reports busy is retried with the current one closed, since a virtual camera built on the webcam (NVIDIA Broadcast over a USB camera, as tested) cannot start while the webcam is held; if it still will not start the previous camera is reopened, and failing that the camera is turned off and announced.

N04 keeps the latest mute intent separate from a particular MediaStreamTrack. Adopting a delayed or replacement microphone applies the current choice, and captured streams arriving after destruction are stopped.

Remote speaking levels come from synchronization-source audio metadata; only the local microphone needs a Web Audio analyser. Samples run every 120 ms with a 500 ms hold, and publish to the UI only when speaking state changes.
Camera/screen prompts, peer signals and teardown have owned lifetimes. testMicrophone opens a local level meter without sending media anywhere and returns an explicit stop operation.

Each call keeps a log of every step (call settings, setup sent and received, each route found by kind and protocol, ICE and connection states, failures that were silent before) with no address or SDP. A connection not up after 15 s, or failed, is diagnosed from the routes each side offered (signalling, no ICE servers, no public route here or there, needs a relay), shown as the peer's trouble, reported to the server, and retried up to twice with the call settings read afresh and an ICE restart from the offering side. The module is loaded only when someone joins a call.

entries.summary: Says which microphone and camera to open, and lists the devices to choose from.
details: microphoneConstraints and cameraConstraints are the one place a huddle's capture constraints are written. A saved device is asked for loosely, so one left unplugged falls back to the default instead of failing the join; a device chosen just now is asked for exactly, so a failure is reported rather than another device opening silently. Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain are on unless turned off. Cameras are asked for with resizeMode crop-and-scale: without it Chromium handed over a virtual camera's full 1080p, past the 1280 cap, which a mesh would send to everyone.

listMediaDevices drops Chromium's 'default' and 'communications' stand-ins, numbers devices whose names the browser keeps back before permission, and names what the system default currently is. canChooseSpeaker detects setSinkId.

entries.summary: Explains microphone, camera and screen-capture failures in actionable language.
details: captureFailure maps browser error names and secure-context availability to advice about permissions, missing devices, competing apps or HTTPS.

Cancelled screen pickers and dismissed camera prompts can return no error message, while a microphone refusal explains why a huddle cannot start. The function is pure enough to test without actually requesting hardware.

entries.summary: Keeps notification eligibility and message visibility rules consistent across shells.
details: decideNotification rejects own messages, inaccessible channels, muted/nothing preferences and active Do Not Disturb before deciding whether a DM, named mention or broadcast should ring.
An @here broadcast applies only to a live message, so an old replay does not notify people as if they had been present when it was sent.
isMessageOnScreen accounts for focus, covered timelines and the exact open thread. notificationBody converts mentions and labelled links to readable words and supplies an attachment-only description.

entries.summary: Exports the reusable React application and shell contracts.
details: Web and desktop entry points import App and the relevant Platform adapter through this package boundary.
The file exposes selected hosting, discovery, backup and saved-server types without requiring consumers to import individual UI implementation files.

entries.summary: Connects React components to the active platform and workspace client.
details: PlatformContext supplies storage and shell capabilities; ClientContext supplies the current WorkspaceClient. Missing providers fail explicitly instead of returning an unusable object.
useWorkspace subscribes to a selected Zustand slice, so an unrelated part of the replica need not rerender the component. OpenMessageContext lets message links navigate inside the existing workspace.

entries.summary: Defines the browser/desktop capability boundary and implements the browser adapter.
details: Platform describes acknowledged storage reads/writes and optional atomic initialization, outbox/draft/record merges and watchers. Optional discovery, hosting, backup and deep-link capabilities let one UI run in both shells.

webPlatform maps those storage operations onto deviceStore. Strict reads preserve unreadability as an error; ordinary optional reads can return null on failure, which matters to caller policies such as the pending Q04 issue.
Browser notifications honor permission and a deduplication tag, while notification clicks refocus the window and run navigation. Downloads use a scoped URL through a hidden no-referrer iframe.
Browser deep links are consumed from the URL fragment and removed after recognition. Desktop adapters can register capture and persist phases for normal close preparation.

entries.summary: Owns application startup, remembered sign-ins and switching between workspaces.
details: The Session union distinguishes loading, failed restore, joining and a connected workspace. Startup strictly parses saved credentials; a corrupt or unavailable store offers retry instead of turning saved sign-ins into an empty list.

Opening a workspace destroys the previous WorkspaceClient, creates a fresh one, connects it, and records the last-use ordering. Deep links can target an already open workspace or carry a pending message target through sign-in.
Appearance, error boundaries, confirmations and toast providers wrap the app. JoinScreen and the desktop-only HostDialog load on demand rather than adding to every returning user's initial download.

Navigation and save versions fence several stale completions inside this window. Q05 remains open: saving the entire remembered-server list from a stale window can revive forgotten credentials or erase another window's newly saved sign-in.

entries.summary: Guides discovery, address probing, saved-token reconnect and password-based joining.
details: A browser quietly recognizes the workspace serving its own origin; desktop discovery subscribes to LAN announcements. Hosted-but-stopped workspaces can offer resume instead of an endless connection attempt.

Address probing normalizes the input and checks application/protocol compatibility before presenting authentication. A probe-attempt number rejects success from an ordinary cancelled or superseded address probe.
Saved sign-ins first validate their token and fall back to a password card when expired. The auth form handles registration, invites and initial-owner claiming through the typed API.

Q06 remains open: the saved-token path and an abandoned password form still lack the same completion ownership as ordinary probes, so late success can invoke the connected callback after the user moved on.

Where the server advertises guest_allowed, Join as guest comes first and asks only for a display name, beside Sign in and Create account. An answer to an abandoned or superseded attempt is ignored, and a refusal leaves the form ready to retry.

entries.summary: Assembles conversation navigation, panels, dialogs, calls and notifications.
details: Provides the active client and gates account-local consumers through WorkspaceStorageGate. The central conversation combines Sidebar, MessageTimeline, Composer and an optional thread, members or utility panel.
Only one side panel is selected at a time. Persistent places such as channels, threads, saved panels and account sections map to route/history state; transient forms and pickers stay component state.

The screen tracks what is truly visible and focused when deciding notifications and read acknowledgement. Missed messages are grouped through CatchUpSummary, and live messages can be announced politely to a screen reader.

Admin dialogs, search, scheduling, profile forms, the keyboard shortcuts list and the video stage use lazy imports with recoverable wrappers. Responsive layout uses a navigation drawer and panel isolation on smaller screens.

N04 routes the Getting started huddle action through the same preference-aware join path as the header, with a stillWanted guard for changed or unmounted navigation. The Q report separately identifies remaining search, Pins and Profile lifetime issues.

entries.summary: Defines the shared visual system, responsive layout and accessibility styling.
details: Semantic surface, ink, accent, border and alert tokens support Onyx, White and system appearance. Density attributes adjust message and sidebar spacing without changing component behavior.

The stylesheet centralizes font, spacing, radius and focus conventions, plus compact-window/drawer behavior and motion-related presentation. UI theme controls and native shell colors are intended to stay consistent with these tokens.
Theme tests check the project's chosen type/radius scale and color contrast; these checks support consistency without replacing manual usability inspection.

entries.summary: Owns browser durability, atomic multi-tab merges and unfinished-write recovery.
details: Each IndexedDB read/merge/write occurs inside one readwrite transaction across the values and made object stores. Transaction completion is the write acknowledgement; other tabs cannot interleave a lost update between the read and write.

Before an asynchronous write, a synchronous localStorage journal records the operation with tab and sequence identity. Restart replays unfinished operations in order; per-key made metadata prevents a replay from repeating an already committed older change.

N02 persists backend ownership before migration and prefers IndexedDB even without BroadcastChannel. A failed, blocked or timed-out open reports unreadability and permits a later retry instead of opening an apparently empty alternate store.

Legacy drafts keep conflicting versions, legacy outboxes merge with tombstones and compaction floors, and copied notification choices keep the more private value. Unrecognized conflicting legacy copies remain until explicit replacement; retirement checks the exact captured legacy text before removal.

BroadcastChannel carries change messages when usable; otherwise storage events carry only a key invalidation and re-read the authoritative backend. Focus also refreshes watchers, and generation guards prevent an older asynchronous refresh from winning.

LocalStorage-only support is reserved for profiles that have not adopted IndexedDB. Later ownership changes block legacy writes and mark watcher data unreadable. Journaling can still fail if localStorage has no room, and N02 does not fix the higher-level Q02/Q03/Q04/Q05 caller races.

entries.summary: Scopes local work to authenticated workspace/account identity and migrates old address keys.
details: workspaceStorageKey creates an encoded local:v1 key from the ready snapshot's workspace ID, user ID, data kind and optional conversation suffix. Older address-and-account keys are retained as migration candidates.

Strict reads validate version envelopes. Only addresses explicitly linked on this device may supply legacy work, preventing an arbitrary server claiming public IDs from automatically reading another address's old drafts.

Per-platform key queues serialize operations within a window; platform atomic merge hooks provide the stronger boundary across windows. Outbox and draft initialization merges preserve concurrent work instead of overwriting a whole map.

At-once draft merges allow pagehide and normal desktop capture to ask for final work immediately. Watch helpers unwrap records into client data, while unreadable saved values reject rather than being treated as first-use absence.

entries.summary: Records the addresses allowed to share one account's stable local workspace data.
details: Address normalization preserves protocol, port and path and rejects credentials, query strings and fragments. These distinctions can identify different servers and therefore cannot be discarded for trust.

The first known address is registered; later aliases require explicit trustWorkspaceAddress approval. Strict parsing of the stored address list refuses damage, while a read-only helper returns only known aliases.

Q02 remains open: the first registration currently uses separate read/write operations behind a per-Platform queue. Two windows can both observe absence and automatically admit different addresses; this needs conditional initialization at the storage owner.

entries.summary: Tells the composer when a queued message's words have durable local ownership.
details: A WeakMap ledger tracks persistence owners and waiters by client and nonce. DraftPersistence acknowledges stored or unsaved outcomes when the outbox, recovery record or delivered message supplies evidence.

whenKeptLocally waits up to five seconds only when a keeper exists; removing the last keeper settles remaining waits as unsaved. This prevents a UI promise from waiting forever after its persistence component disappears.

entries.summary: Stores how much each account's desktop notification may reveal.
details: full shows author/conversation and message text, sender hides the message text, and none removes names and conversation detail. Catch-up notifications apply the same privacy choice.

Strict initial reads, damaged-entry validation and an unknown-account marker default unreadable choices to none. Atomic record merges change one account at a time and watchers apply another window's saved choice.

Q03 remains open: an older initial-read or save reply can overwrite a newer private watch update in the active window. Durable storage can remain private while the in-memory choice regresses; N02 backend durability alone does not resolve this ordering.

entries.summary: Keeps how huddles start on this device: join muted, and the chosen devices.
details: A per-Platform shared Zustand store loads the device preference strictly and validates its boolean shape. Unknown or damaged preferences expose retry and keep the microphone off.

Join waits while initialization or saving is pending, then checks whether the caller still wants this channel and whether the client remains usable. N04 fences old reads with a load version so a retry or acknowledged explicit choice wins.
A confirmed absent record is handled as a first-use default; the conservative muted state applies while the record is unresolved or unreadable.

The same record keeps the chosen microphone, camera and speaker ids and the three microphone processing switches. Only keys that were chosen are written; on load a field of the wrong type is dropped rather than making the whole record unreadable. joinHuddle passes the microphone and camera choices to the session.

entries.summary: Lists devices for the pickers and applies a device choice to a call in progress.
details: useMediaDevices lists microphones, cameras and speakers, again on devicechange and on demand once a permission grant makes names available.

chooseDevices switches the live huddle first (microphone or camera) and saves the choice only once the device opened, so a failed choice rejects and changes nothing. useSpeaker routes an audio element through the chosen speaker with setSinkId.

entries.summary: Checks a TURN relay gives this computer a route, the way a call would ask.
details: probeRelay opens a connection allowed only relayed routes and offers a data channel so it gathers them; a relay candidate means the relay answered and took the username and password.
A 401 from the relay reads as a refused password, anything else as a relay this computer could not reach; it gives up after ten seconds and always closes the connection.

entries.summary: Shares the Enter-to-send choice across composers on this device.
details: The store begins with Enter creating a newline until the initial preference read answers, and updates the selected choice only after a successful save.

A loaded boolean chooses the behavior; absence uses the current default. Q04 remains open because this caller uses a non-strict browser read, allowing read refusal to appear as absence and unexpectedly enable Enter-to-send.

entries.summary: Loads and applies the device's theme and message density.
details: A shared store validates system/dark/light and comfortable/compact values and supplies existing defaults for absent or obsolete settings.
A choice appears immediately and rolls back on save failure with a message. useApplyAppearance writes document data attributes consumed by theme.css so all screens follow the same choice.

entries.summary: Turns account refusal codes and session user agents into readable labels.
details: accountError distinguishes changed credentials, expired sessions, role restrictions and invalid password changes instead of showing raw API codes.
deviceLabel derives a coarse browser/app and operating-system name for the Devices list. It does not claim to identify an exact physical device.

entries.summary: Defines the routable Account settings sections.
details: The ordered list names profile, notifications, appearance, composing, calls, security, devices and storage.
isAccountSection validates an untrusted route value before AccountDialog uses it.

entries.summary: Represents workspace places in the URL and browser history.
details: A WorkspaceRoute combines a channel with one optional thread or side panel and a persistent dialog. Strict token and enum parsing refuses malformed hashes or unsupported account sections.
History state is bound to the workspace server, so an entry from one connected workspace cannot choose a channel in another. Fresh browser hashes are accepted only for the workspace serving the page.
writeRoute adds a Back/Forward step for normal movement and replaces automatic or initial corrections. Phone drawer state stays in history rather than becoming a shareable link.
ReadingPosition stores a message ID and viewport offset in the current history entry. Late position updates check the server/channel so an old scroller cannot rewrite a newer destination.

entries.summary: Parses and builds join/message links and chooses an address suitable for sharing.
details: Supports Tandem desktop schemes, legacy schemes and browser fragment forms. Browser invite codes sit in the fragment, which is not sent as the HTTP request target or Referer fragment.

shareableServer prefers a live temporary address owned by this desktop, then a published server address, usable LAN addresses or the connected non-loopback address. It marks links that reach only the current computer as localOnly.
Address formatting preserves the destination when shortening display text; LAN ranking favors ordinary home/office interfaces over common virtual-network addresses.

entries.summary: Shares deep-link scheme constants and safe address normalization.
details: Re-exports current and accepted legacy schemes from protocol.
normalizeServerUrlSafe returns null for invalid user input so parsing and discovery helpers can discard bad candidates without throwing through the UI.

entries.summary: Distinguishes reachability, credentials, mixed-content and version problems.
details: connectionFailure uses status, browser protocol and timeout identity to recommend the appropriate action.
incompatibleWorkspace checks the application marker and protocol version before authentication and states which side needs an update. Repeated network retry cannot correct a protocol mismatch.

entries.summary: Strictly validates remembered workspace credentials before restoring them.
details: Checks list shape, nonempty tokens, presentation fields, nonnegative last-use time and HTTP(S) URL shape.
Unreadable data throws instead of becoming an empty list that a later save could overwrite. This read guard is useful even though the multi-window whole-list write race Q05 remains open in App.

entries.summary: Recognizes a remembered workspace hosted here that is currently stopped.
details: Matches a saved loopback address and explicit port against lastHosted; repeated workspace names are not identity.
Checks hosting phase to avoid offering resume while starting/stopping, and a failed optional status read retains normal connection behavior.

entries.summary: Shares live native hosting status and the most recently hosted workspace.
details: useHostingStatus combines status reads and native subscriptions. A revision ensures a newer live update takes precedence over an older request result.
Refresh retains the existing status instead of blanking controls, and useLastHosted rereads after relevant hosting changes while ignoring results from a disposed effect.

entries.summary: Defines docked, expanded and hidden call presentation and detects visible video.
details: huddleHasVideo checks local camera/share and every peer's camera/share stream.
This small presentation rule keeps screen layout independent from the WebRTC transport implementation.

entries.summary: Exposes source identity embedded by web and desktop builds.
details: Reads the build-time stamp safely when it exists and returns null for development/tests without one.
describeBuild renders a short revision and dirty-source indication for diagnostics so a running artifact can be compared with validation evidence.

entries.summary: Constructs a previewable operating report without including message contents.
details: Reports source/protocol versions, connection status, pending-send count, huddle connection counts, notification capability and device/window information.

Owner/admin operating status adds database and attachment sizes, queue lengths, retention progress, disk space and event-loop timing. It reports quantities and failures rather than quoting queued messages or secrets.
The report filename uses time rather than a workspace/person name; copying or saving remains an explicit UI action.

Formats the device's call log line by line in UTC, and the server's call log as joins, leaves, setups passed on or dropped, and each side's report with its routes, servers, ICE state and cause in words.

entries.summary: Groups replayed missed messages into an occasional notification summary.
details: Holds eligible messages by ID until replay is quiet for one second, with at most one summary every two minutes by default.
Before showing, stillNews rechecks read state, notification policy and access; deleted held messages can be dropped. This reduces a reconnect burst to a useful summary instead of many interruptions.

entries.summary: Bounds refresh work for lists receiving many invalidation signals.
details: soon merges a burst into one delayed request, or one queued refresh after a request already running. now cancels obsolete work and loads the current selection immediately.
At most one request runs and one refresh waits. stop cancels timers and owned transfers while allowing a subsequently reopened view to load again.

entries.summary: Remembers the last conversation for this authenticated account on this device.
details: Uses the stable workspace/account key and validates a channel token when restoring. undefined means still loading and null means no usable memory.
Repeated writes to the same destination are avoided. A failed save costs a later navigation click and does not block chatting.

entries.summary: Maintains up to ten recent searches within an account's workspace scope.
details: Validates and deduplicates query/channel entries, placing a repeated choice at the front.

A per-platform key queue spans closed and reopened dialogs so an older append cannot undo an explicit clear within that owner. Failure reports that local history is unavailable while server search remains usable.

entries.summary: Subscribes each message row only to the users and channels it actually displays.
details: Extracts author, mention, reaction and linked-channel IDs from message data.

usePick preserves object identity until a referenced entry changes and skips work while the source map is unchanged. Renaming an unrelated person or typing elsewhere therefore need not rerender every visible message.

entries.summary: Centralizes byte/time labels, conversation titles and deterministic avatars.
details: Reusable Intl.DateTimeFormat instances avoid constructing a formatter for every message row. Day labels recognize Today and Yesterday in the reader's local time.
DM titles derive from other participants, and deterministic hues/initials give each account a consistent avatar without image requests.

entries.summary: Provides the shared searchable emoji choices and accessible labels.
details: A small static catalog supplies both the composer chooser and reaction picker.
findEmoji matches descriptive words or a pasted emoji, so the same labels support discovery and button accessibility.

entries.summary: Builds schedule presets and labels using the device's local calendar.
details: Offers relative short delays, a still-future evening, tomorrow at 09:00 and next Monday morning.
localDateTime preserves the local clock for datetime-local fields; formatScheduleTime supplies Today/Tomorrow labels without treating a local calendar date as UTC.

entries.summary: Supplies notification pause durations and readable resume times.
details: Short options compute the deadline when selected, while tomorrow morning is a calendar time rather than an arbitrary twelve-hour delay.
Uses the scheduling formatter for a consistent resume label.

entries.summary: Writes keyboard shortcuts as the person's own keyboard labels them.
details: isApple and modKey choose ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; shortcutLabel turns "Mod+Shift+U" into "⌘⇧U" or "Ctrl Shift U", so hints never name the wrong key.

entries.summary: The statuses people set most, offered wherever a status is chosen.
details: One list of emoji and text presets shared by the profile form and quick status, so both offer the same choices.

entries.summary: Protects input-method composition, code blocks and caret placement.
details: isImeKey checks both isComposing and key code 229, preventing Enter used to choose a Japanese/Chinese/Korean candidate from sending or navigating.
insideCodeBlock leaves Enter as a newline inside an unfinished triple-backtick block.
caretToRestore accepts a formatting/autocomplete position only if the text still matches the rewrite that produced it, so newer typing cannot be displaced by an old caret correction.

entries.summary: Maps stored mention tokens to the readable text a message box shows, and edits back.
details: projectMentions turns <@USER_ID>, <#CHANNEL_ID> and <!here>/<!channel>/<!everyone> into @name, #channel and @here segments. The stored string stays the only source of truth; an unresolved person or channel shows @unknown or #unknown and keeps its ID.

replaceShown applies an edit made to the readable text to the stored text. A mention the edit reaches into becomes the ordinary text of what remains of its label, so editing a name never silently redirects a mention and a typed or pasted name never acquires an ID.

shownEdit recovers the single changed range from before/after text, using the caret to settle ambiguous repeats. storedPosition/shownPosition translate selections, widening a selection inside a mention to the whole token for formatting.

entries.summary: Binds a textarea to readable mentions for both the composer and the message editor.
details: The owner keeps stored text as before (drafts, sends, schedules, outbox and edit conflicts are unchanged strings); the hook supplies the shown value, converts each change event back, and restores the caret only while the shown text still matches.

Rewrites such as a completed mention, emoji or formatting go through document.execCommand(insertText) where available, so the browser's own Undo and Redo take them back. A bounded map from shown to stored text lets historyUndo/historyRedo restore mentions rather than plain names.
Backspace at a mention's end or Delete at its start selects the whole mention first, so one key removes it. Without execCommand (as in jsdom) the stored text is committed directly.

entries.summary: Keeps reading anchors for recently visited threads during this app session.
details: Stores root-specific message/offset positions by workspace address, removing the entry when the reader returns to the newest reply.
The oldest entry is evicted past 100 threads, bounding memory. Unlike channel history state, this cache lasts only for the running app.

entries.summary: Adds desktop Back/Forward keyboard and mouse shortcuts.
details: When enabled, Alt+Left/Right and mouse side buttons call browser history.
Modified or already handled key events are left alone; listeners are removed with the component. Ordinary web browsers already supply this behavior.

entries.summary: Makes responsive decisions react to a changing media query.
details: Initializes from matchMedia when available and subscribes to change events.
The hook rechecks on a query change and removes its listener, keeping viewport-driven component behavior synchronized with CSS.

entries.summary: Copies text and reports success only after a real clipboard operation.
details: Uses Clipboard API first, then a temporary selected textarea for ordinary HTTP LAN pages or refused clipboard permission.

The temporary field lives inside an active dialog when necessary, preserving the focus trap, and restores previous focus after removal. Per-key feedback and a short reset timer keep copy controls truthful.

entries.summary: Keeps suggestion navigation accessible while focus remains in the text field.
details: ArrowUp/Down wrap the selected suggestion and aria-activedescendant tells screen readers which option is active.
Mouse selection avoids stealing the caret. Left/Right/Home/End remain normal editing keys; only keyboard movement scrolls the active suggestion into view.

entries.summary: Moves focus into an opened panel and returns it when the panel closes.
details: A heading receives focus when appropriate; visible disclosure toggles can keep it. Phone panels that cover their opener take focus instead.
Cleanup restores focus only if it stayed inside the closing panel or was lost, using message-row and drawer fallbacks when the original control is no longer focusable.

entries.summary: Turns a long message list into a practical keyboard navigation region.
details: Only the active message and its controls participate in sequential Tab order; arrows, Home and End move between articles, Enter enters actions and Escape returns to the message.
A MutationObserver reapplies the rule when rows or controls change without requiring the whole timeline to rerender. Pointer and reading-cursor access remain available.

entries.summary: Implements consistent WAI-ARIA tab selection and keyboard movement.
details: One selected tab is a Tab stop; Left/Right wrap and Home/End select the endpoints. Each tab and the shared panel have matching IDs and labels.
Selection follows focus because these panels can show content or loading state immediately. Alt/Ctrl/Meta combinations are not intercepted.

entries.summary: Owns visible message text, attachments, mentions, formatting and scheduling intent.
details: Channel and thread composers use different draft keys. Typing updates local React text immediately and hands it to the client after a 250 ms debounce; an untouched composer can receive a restored or other-window draft without overwriting newer typing.

N03 uses layout cleanup plus capture-phase pagehide/visibility/native-close hooks to hand over the actual last visible text before persistence runs. This closes the gap where a final debounced keystroke could disappear on normal navigation or close.

Send validates content and limits, then queues through WorkspaceClient. The words remain owned until localWork acknowledges the send or recovery record, and refusal keeps an actionable notice rather than silently dropping the message.

The composer supports Unicode-aware mention suggestions, slash-command hints, emoji, formatting preview, drag/paste attachments, progress and reply broadcast choice. IME and code-block Enter rules prevent premature actions; pending caret moves are tied to the text they were computed for.

The field shows mentions as names (choosing @here shows @here) through useMentionField, while text, drafts and sends keep <!here> and <@USER_ID>. A mention already completed is not offered again; the character limit counts the stored text the server receives.

Scheduling uploads attachments, persists the exact request including nonce, file IDs and chosen time before posting, and restores unresolved scheduling requests before another send. A retry reuses the original request identity rather than creating a duplicate schedule.

Q04 remains open at the preference caller: unreadability can be converted to an Enter-to-send default. N03 covers normal preparation and persistence acknowledgements, not every power-loss or OS-termination case.

entries.summary: Bridges in-memory unsent work to acknowledged account-scoped storage.
details: Creates stable drafts, outbox and unstored-sends keys from authenticated workspace/account identity. Restores records strictly, then subscribes to client changes and other-window storage changes.

Tracks only this window's draft changes against confirmed base values and only its queued sends/refusals/removals with revisions. Shared merges preserve unrelated work and consume tombstones rather than resurrecting removed sends.

Outbox persistence precedes clearing corresponding durable drafts. If a send was typed and sent before a saved draft existed, a separate unstored-sends recovery record can preserve its words when the outbox write fails.

Recovery restores a nonce's words as a send or a draft according to durable ownership; missing File bytes still remain visibly unavailable. Failed reads and writes show Retry, and an ordinary retry flushes current memory instead of rereading stale disk over newer intent.

For N03's native persist phase, restoration must succeed, current changes are flushed, and all owned writes including recovery follow-up work settle. Confirmed remaining differences and a retained failure prevent a later no-op write from falsely acknowledging lost text.

Pagehide/hidden/unmount ask for immediate flush, while normal desktop close can await acknowledgement. A browser crash relies on the storage journal when available; this file cannot promise that every refused or abruptly interrupted write reached disk.

entries.summary: Keeps local-work components unmounted until the current address is admitted.
details: Reads workspace and account identity from the ready replica, then checks the local trusted-address record. The gate shows checking, explicit approval, saving or retryable error before mounting drafts/search-history consumers.
Approval explains that the address can access saved local work and may resume queued sends. Effects fence results to their current client/workspace/account scope.
The ordinary later-address refusal works, but Q02 documents the separate simultaneous first-registration gap in the trust helper; this gate cannot compensate for an incorrectly admitted address.

entries.summary: Renders an app-owned form with input and result lifetime bound to its view ID.
details: ViewModal keys AppForm by view.id, so a newly arriving app form starts with its own values, field errors, message and busy state.
Inputs are keyed by block and action ID and submitted as a nested payload. Validation refusal keeps the form open and focuses the first refused field.

N05 adds alive and submitting guards plus ID-bound client operations: a previous form's success, failure or dismissal cannot close or contaminate its replacement. Answers are not persisted locally and closing alone does not send a callback.

entries.summary: Shows bounded channel history while preserving reading and scroll position.
details: Loads initial, older and newer history through owned request tickets. A top visible message and offset anchor preserve position while prepending rows; explicit message jumps center and highlight a target.
Readers at the latest message stay pinned as content or viewport size changes; readers looking back are not pulled to the bottom. History entries remember where a conversation was being read.

Separately renders optimistic pending sends with Retry/Discard and ephemeral app answers with dismissal/limit notices. Date dividers, an unread boundary and typing indicators make the timeline understandable.

Read acknowledgement follows a genuinely visible tail, and useRovingMessages makes the list a manageable keyboard region. The actual row count is bounded in client-core rather than claiming full DOM virtualization.

entries.summary: Renders one message and its authorized actions with narrow replica subscriptions.
details: The memoized row renders author, timestamps, mrkdwn, files, reactions, thread affordances and app buttons. useMessageReferences tracks only referenced users/channels, and self identity/role controls relevant actions.

Reaction, pin and saved toggles report refused optimistic changes through a toast with a repeatable intent. Delete uses an explicit confirmation; mark unread delegates channel or thread cursor behavior to the client.

Copying text/link waits for clipboard outcome. App link buttons navigate normally while interactive buttons call the app through the server and wait for its result; permissions remain enforced by the server.
The in-place editor is a lazy chunk with an inline loading status and a recoverable failure, keeping editing code out of the entry every visit downloads.

entries.summary: Edits a message while preserving unsaved words and the original comparison base.
details: An edit draft has its own message-specific slot and stores both text and the message text it began from, including compatibility with older plain-text drafts.
Save uses expectedText so a concurrent edit can be refused instead of being overwritten unnoticed. Formatting, preview, IME and code-block behavior match the composer.
The box and the Current message shown on an edit conflict read mentions as names; the kept {text, base} and the saved text keep their tokens. MessageItem loads the editor on first use.

entries.summary: Displays a root message, paged replies and an independent reply composer.
details: Loads the root's thread through WorkspaceClient, displays optimistic replies and manages retry/discard for waiting sends.

Remembers reply reading anchors, protects current thread history from eviction and acknowledges the thread cursor when appropriate. Follow/Unfollow calls the client's thread-follow logic; Q09 documents its remaining request-order race.
A thread composer uses a root-specific draft key and optional also-send-to-channel choice rather than clobbering the channel composer.

entries.summary: Shares the layout and loading behavior for Pins, Saved and followed Threads.
details: The generic panel renders server-loaded message sets, row context, counts, loading/empty/refusal state and an explicit Refresh action.
Pins are channel-specific, Saved spans readable conversations, and Threads represents followed conversations with unread counts and opens the thread rather than a single message.

Q08 remains open: Pins invalidation currently depends on loaded timeline pins, so a deleted pinned row from an unloaded timeline can remain until Refresh. Previously fetched panel text should not be described as always live.

entries.summary: Searches server-side message text and attachment names with understandable filters.
details: Displays search modifiers and the parsed interpretation, scope/date/file-type controls, pagination, matched terms and attachment-name reasons for a result.
Recent searches are kept in the authenticated local scope; choosing a result requests an in-app message jump rather than treating a result excerpt as the whole conversation.

Q07 remains open: results are copied into dialog state and do not yet reliably invalidate for deletion, retention or edit events. Repeating the search updates them; an open result list must not be described as an authoritative live replica.

entries.summary: Lists unread or mentioned messages with paged, coalesced refreshes.
details: Filter tabs reset cursor paging; read cursors, thread follows, mention counts and retention state signal changes that can require fresh activity.
A 250 ms CoalescedLoader merges bursts, cancels obsolete selection requests and preserves existing content during refresh. Rows can jump to or deliberately mark a conversation read.

entries.summary: Shows queued, held and failed schedules and lets the author resolve them.
details: Loads server-owned schedules and presents future delivery times, status and attachment context.
Supports editing/rescheduling, cancelling and returning words to the appropriate draft. Server scheduling uses request identity, while the client preserves actionable refusal and refresh state.

entries.summary: Displays file cards, lazy authenticated image previews and full-size lightboxes.
details: Image loading begins near the viewport using IntersectionObserver, then retains/releases the shared FileCache resource. Large or non-image files use cards and scoped download URLs instead of eager inline transfer.

A resource is bound to the active client/file and can show loading, failure, retry or invalidated state. N10 cache notices make open previews become unavailable when their owner message/thread is removed.

Pending attachments use temporary local previews; lightboxes share the modal focus layer. The UI distinguishes a failed download from successful handoff rather than claiming the browser/OS completed it.

entries.summary: Renders the supported Slack-style message syntax into React elements.
details: Handles fenced and inline code, bold/italic/strike, quotes, user/channel references and ordinary or labelled HTTP links without interpreting message text as arbitrary HTML.

Resolves mentions against supplied users/channels, with the same labels the composer shows (mentionDocument), and opens a message link in-place only when it belongs to a known address of this workspace.
A labelled link that looks like a different host exposes the actual destination. Code/quote edge trimming avoids artificial blank lines around block elements.

entries.summary: Shares formatting transformations, shortcuts and message length limits.
details: formatText wraps or inserts syntax and returns the corresponding selection so composer/editor behavior stays consistent.
The toolbar supplies supported formatting and preview affordances; formattingShortcut and MESSAGE_LIMIT keep keyboard handling and validation aligned.

entries.summary: Makes the shared emoji catalog searchable for a message reaction.
details: Uses listbox selection and labelled buttons so keyboard, screen-reader and pointer users can choose the same emoji.
Touch users tap before opening the software keyboard, allowing the picker to show choices without the keyboard immediately covering them.

entries.summary: Combines workspace switching, conversation navigation, unread context and account actions.
details: A compact workspace rail and workspace menu expose remembered workspaces without presenting saved tokens to the visible navigation.
Channel and DM rows show unread/muted/activity state and choose destinations supplied by the workspace screen. Admin actions appear only where the current account can use them.
Snooze controls compute actual resume times and use the client's latest-choice behavior. Menu grouping saves vertical space so short windows retain room for conversations.
A guest's sidebar leaves out Friends, Scheduled, New channel and direct messages, says Guest under the name, and offers Create an account in place of invites and account settings.

entries.summary: Provides Ctrl+K navigation to channels, DMs and people.
details: Builds labelled suggestion rows and keeps text-field focus with useListbox; IME Enter stays text input.
Existing conversations navigate directly, while a person without a DM starts one and shows pending/failure state. This is a navigation convenience over the server-authorized openDm operation.

entries.summary: Shows the active conversation's people grouped by online presence.
details: DMs use their known participant IDs; channels fetch membership when opened and ignore results after disposal.
Active users are sorted by name, grouped online/offline and linked to profiles. Shared loading and focus helpers make failure/retry and dismissal consistent.

entries.summary: Edits channel details and manages membership, managers and notification choices.
details: Presents topic/description and member controls under shared channel permission rules; the server remains responsible for enforcement.
Updates, inviting/removing members, changing managers and leaving map API refusals into readable actions. Channel notification writes expose retry rather than silently abandoning a refused choice.

entries.summary: Groups channel creation/browsing, new conversations and invite management forms.
details: NewChannelDialog creates public/private channels; BrowseChannelsDialog lists and joins available channels; NewDmDialog chooses participants and opens a direct/group conversation.
InviteDialog creates shareable invite links, lists their status and lets permitted users revoke them. Clipboard outcome and readable server refusal state are preserved.
These occasional forms are lazy-loaded by the workspace screen rather than required for every returning conversation view.
GuestAccountDialog keeps a guest's identity as an account; the new session token reopens the workspace as the same person.

entries.summary: Displays a person's profile and provides the shared self-profile editor.
details: ProfileForm updates the current user's name and status through Api. Another person's profile can start/open a direct message.
Q11 remains open: dismissing Profile during its Message action does not yet end navigation ownership, so the old completion can navigate after a later channel choice.

entries.summary: Lists contacts and friend-request actions within the workspace.
details: FriendActions requests, accepts or removes a relationship through Api and displays current request state.
The list resolves workspace people and supports opening their profiles or conversations; relationship state belongs to the server-backed replica.

entries.summary: Collects account, device and presentation settings in routable sections.
details: Section keyboard navigation and route callbacks connect profile, notifications, appearance, composing, calls, security, devices and storage to Back/Forward history.
Uses shared preference stores for notification preview, Enter behavior, appearance and join-muted choice. Calls includes a local microphone check and N04 retry for unreadable call preferences.
Security and Devices change passwords, list/revoke sessions and sign out through the server; Storage displays server usage. Confirmation identifies destructive session changes.
The settings UI does not itself fix remaining Q03/Q04 preference ordering/read-policy issues; those are tracked in their underlying helper entries.

entries.summary: Lets administrators inspect accounts and manage access under server role rules.
details: Loads all users, offers role/deactivation/invite-permission actions, password reset and ownership transfer where permitted.

PersonMenu consolidates row actions into one accessible menu. Confirmations and mapped refusal messages communicate lost access, protected ownership and equal-admin restrictions; hidden buttons are not treated as authorization.

entries.summary: Manages bot apps, webhooks, commands, subscriptions and callback configuration.
details: Creates and removes integrations and exposes explicit credential replacement actions. Bot tokens shown once stay only in this UI session; rereadable secrets have reveal/copy controls.
Configures slash commands, event subscriptions and verified interactivity URLs; refreshes composer command hints when those change.
Delivery status distinguishes waiting, given-up and never-queued events and offers retry where supported. The integration contract link explains supported behavior and differences from Slack.

entries.summary: Shows paged administrator changes as readable audit sentences.
details: Looks up current names from stored IDs and defensively interprets details, so newer or partial records remain understandable.
Loads only when requested, pages through the server audit log and preserves keyboard focus when the final page removes a pagination control.

entries.summary: Controls desktop hosting, workspace folders, backup/restore and public reachability.
details: The browser does not own a server; native Platform.hosting provides the operations this dialog presents. Existing workspace folders and new workspace names are separate start intents.
Presents running/stopped/startup status, port and rename controls, LAN and public-address choices, connector failure and launch recovery actions.
Lists hosted workspaces and backup schedules, supports backup/restore and explains a restored copy's pending apps, schedules, deliveries and sessions before activation.

N11/N12 fixes live in the desktop registry/controller: restored safety holds survive damaged metadata and cleanup ownership gates reopening. The dialog exposes those statuses; pending Q12/Q13 startup/queue gaps must not be claimed solved by the UI.

Who may join is two choices, Require an account to join and, under it, Require an invite link; clearing the first lets visitors join as guests. Before opening the choice travels with openToAll; while open it is applied with setAccessPolicy and shown as the workspace acknowledges it.

entries.summary: The Calls from other networks card in Manage hosting: no relay, Cloudflare, or another TURN server.
details: Shows the saved relay without its secret; a token or password left empty keeps the saved one for the same key or username. Save reaches calls that start afterwards.

Test asks the app for the relay servers a call would be given and runs probeRelay, saying whether the relay works, refused the password, or could not be reached. A refusal calls found out about since is shown as an alert.

entries.summary: Keeps known workspace addresses ready before the user copies a link.
details: Combines server-info, native hosting status and explicitly trusted aliases to choose a sharing address without awaiting a network request in the clipboard click handler.
Rechecks after reconnect, foreground return and periodically while open so temporary/public addresses can refresh. Context also tells Mrkdwn which workspace message links can navigate in-place.

entries.summary: Shows setup steps that complete from actual workspace/account behavior.
details: Tracks creating a channel, inviting someone, enabling notifications and participating in a huddle, with account/workspace-local dismissal memory.
The checklist can disappear after completion or explicit dismissal. N04's screen wiring makes its huddle action use the preference-aware join operation.

entries.summary: Requests browser notification permission from an intentional visible gesture.
details: Appears after sign-in rather than asking from an unrelated first click. Not now defers the banner for two weeks on this device.
An explicit browser denial remains quiet until site permission changes, and the native desktop notification adapter does not need this banner.

entries.summary: Politely announces new visible messages without flooding a screen reader.
details: A single arrival includes a bounded excerpt; a burst groups count and up to a few sender names after a quiet period.
Announcements do not steal focus, and navigation clears old-conversation waiting messages so they are not announced in the new destination.

entries.summary: Header control that starts a huddle, joins the running one, or says you are in it.
details: Names the action by the room's state (Start a huddle, Join the huddle (n), In huddle) and joins through the same preference-aware path as other entry points.

entries.summary: Shows call presence, speaking rings and the header join/start control.
details: HuddleFace resolves participants and speaking state, while the compact bar hosts controls and a way to restore hidden video.
HuddleButton starts or joins through the shared call-preference store and provides meaningful error state. N04 makes this header path agree with Getting started about mute initialization.
Once a peer's connection has a diagnosed trouble, the bar says Can't connect to them and offers Why? See the call log.

entries.summary: Provides shared microphone, camera, screen-share and leave actions.
details: Used by both the compact bar and fullscreen stage so the call actions stay available in either layout.
Stable accessible names plus aria-pressed describe toggles; captureFailure distinguishes a cancelled picker from a permission/device problem. A lost microphone exposes retry.

Beside Mute and Camera, a small arrow opens a menu of microphones and speakers, or cameras, with the chosen one ticked (menuitemradio) and a link to Voice & video settings. The menus are left out of the full-screen overlay, because menus open on the page beneath a fullscreen element.

entries.summary: Keeps each remote microphone playing independently of video layout.
details: Peer audio elements attach microphone streams even when the call has no camera or the video stage is hidden.
Playback refusal produces a recovery action; one user gesture retries blocked peers while already audible streams are left intact. This avoids duplicate audio from video elements.
Each peer's audio element plays through the speaker chosen in Voice & video settings.

entries.summary: Arranges cameras and shares into docked, gallery, presenting or spotlight views.
details: stageItems prioritizes screen shares then participants; bestFit tries column counts to find the largest 16:9 tiles for the actual container dimensions.
Video surfaces stay muted because HuddleAudio owns voices. Local self-video and remote camera/share streams display without opening a second media capture.
Resize observation updates layout, and accessible tiles/actions expose focus, fullscreen and share controls. Lazy loading keeps the stage out of initial conversation downloads until needed.

entries.summary: Lets the user test local microphone level before joining a huddle.
details: Opens the chosen microphone with the chosen processing through client-core's testMicrophone, shows its name and level, and opens it again when the choice changes. An optional playback sends the voice to the chosen speaker.
Nothing is sent to peers or the server. Stopping the check or closing settings stops the captured tracks.

entries.summary: The Voice & video section of Account settings: devices, processing and tests.
details: Microphone, speaker (where setSinkId exists) and camera pickers with the system default first; a chosen device that is unplugged stays listed as such. Changes apply to a huddle in progress through chooseDevices and are kept for every workspace on this device.

Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic volume switches, a microphone test with playback, a two-tone speaker test, a mirrored camera preview, and join-muted. When the browser keeps device names back it offers to ask for the microphone once.

entries.summary: Shows the complete diagnostics report before copying or downloading it.
details: Reads server-info and optional owner/admin operating status, recording a readable failure when either is unavailable.
The person can inspect the report and choose copy or local text-file save; the dialog does not send diagnostics to another service.
The report includes this device's call log and, for the owner and admins, the server's call log, with people named by handle. Opened from a call that cannot connect, it starts at the call log.

entries.summary: Lists and filters keyboard shortcuts using the current composing preference.
details: Writing-key descriptions change with Enter-to-send so the help reflects active behavior.
A query matches words across keys and explanations, exposing navigation, message, formatting and call shortcuts without requiring the reader to memorize them.

entries.summary: Draws consistent initials avatars and presence indicators without image downloads.
details: Avatar uses the account's deterministic hue and display-name initials; missing users receive a fallback.
PresenceDot and AvatarWithPresence draw online state with a ring matching the parent surface, keeping the same visual rule across rows and calls.

entries.summary: Provides the application's small inline SVG icon vocabulary and brand mark.
details: IconName maps to shared vector paths, stroke/size conventions and accessible usage supplied by parent controls.
Inline vectors avoid an icon font, extra network fetch and a large icon runtime dependency while keeping common controls visually consistent.

entries.summary: Centralizes primary, secondary, danger and quiet action styling.
details: buttonClass lets existing native buttons reuse variants; Button forwards native attributes and ref.
Preserves native button semantics, including form submission unless type=button is explicitly chosen.

entries.summary: Owns the shared stack of modal portals and keyboard/focus isolation.
details: Tracks the active layer, makes the page and older portals inert, and permits only the top layer to handle Escape, outside dismissal and tab containment.

Focus restoration follows connected usable openers and fallback owners even if an underlying dialog was removed. Layout registration accounts for child autoFocus occurring before portal ownership is fully installed.
Central ownership avoids competing independent focus traps for dialogs, menus and lightboxes.

entries.summary: Adds standard dialog structure and form styling on top of Modal.
details: Supplies a titled surface, accessible description relationship, close affordance and configurable width.
Exports shared input classes so forms use the same focus, border and disabled appearance.

entries.summary: A small panel anchored to the control that opened it, such as Send later's choices.
details: Built on the modal layer like Menu: Escape or a press outside closes it, the page beneath waits, and focus returns to the control. It sits above the control, or below when there is no room, and follows it as the page scrolls.

entries.summary: Provides one accessible compact menu for row and workspace actions.
details: Built on the modal layer, with arrow navigation, Enter selection, Escape/outside dismissal and focus return to the trigger.
Repositions with scrolling instead of abandoning an action when a live timeline shifts. Destructive and disabled items keep consistent presentation.

entries.summary: Explains compact controls without taking focus or blocking the page.
details: Hover opens after a short delay; keyboard focus opens immediately; Escape dismisses the hint. The floating portal follows its trigger and flips when needed.
Composes event handlers, accessible descriptions and refs, including React ref-cleanup behavior, so decorating a control does not replace its own lifetime contract.

entries.summary: Asks named questions for irreversible user actions and returns a boolean answer.
details: ConfirmProvider and useConfirm expose a promise resolved true only by the explicitly named action; cancellation, closing and Escape resolve false.
A destructive question begins on Cancel and can explain the consequence. Callers act on the answer rather than inferring permission from dismissal.

entries.summary: Reports operation outcomes without interrupting current input.
details: Success notices clear after a reading interval, while failures remain for acknowledgement and can offer an operation-specific retry or undo.
A bounded stack pauses countdowns during hover/focus and preserves a nearby focus destination when a notice is removed. Notices never make the workspace inert.

entries.summary: Keeps loading, refresh, empty and retry state consistent across lists.
details: Before first content it renders varied stand-in rows; later refreshes keep the current list and show a status line.

A stable live region and layout cleanup preserve focus when a Retry/empty-state action is replaced by results. This is a shared usability primitive rather than each panel inventing its own state layout.

entries.summary: Contains a broken React view while preserving the workspace connection and typed work.
details: Catches render failures and supplies recoverable fallback controls at the relevant boundary.
Dismissal can retry the same tree without automatically reloading the whole app, allowing the live client and unsent state outside that boundary to remain owned.

entries.summary: Wraps on-demand panels and dialogs with loading and failed-chunk recovery.
details: Suspense announces what is loading and retains a way to close the pending view.
An ErrorBoundary confines a failed download to that view and provides close/reload actions, allowing the rest of the workspace to remain usable.

flows.title: From typing a message to a confirmed row
flows.summary: The visible draft, durable local work and server message each have different owners. Sending connects them with a nonce and acknowledgement rather than merely clearing the textarea.

steps.title: Type and protect the draft
steps.description: Composer updates local text immediately, debounces client.setDraft for ordinary typing, and captures current text before navigation or normal close. Thread replies use their own draft key.

steps.title: Queue an optimistic send
steps.description: WorkspaceClient validates admission, generates a random nonce, appends PendingMessage and creates local attachment previews. The 50-send limit refuses extra work while keeping the draft.

steps.title: Acquire durable ownership
steps.description: DraftPersistence merges the outbox before clearing the corresponding saved draft. localWork settles the nonce after storage or delivery evidence; failures retain retry/recovery state.

steps.title: Upload and post
steps.description: deliver uploads chosen files, caches successful upload IDs for a retry and posts the exact message request. Progress belongs to the pending row.

steps.title: Reconcile server evidence
steps.description: The HTTP response or WebSocket message.created event updates the replica and removes the optimistic entry by nonce. File previews are released and durable removal creates an outbox tombstone.

flows.title: Reconnect, restart and unfinished-write recovery
flows.summary: Recovery distinguishes unknown network outcome, explicit server refusal and unavailable local attachment bytes. The same text must not silently become two sends.

steps.title: Keep uncertainty visible
steps.description: A failed send stays in pending state with an actionable reason. A known refusal requires deliberate Retry; an uncertain outcome retains the same nonce.

steps.title: Journal before asynchronous persistence
steps.description: deviceStore synchronously records the storage operation, then commits an IndexedDB transaction. Failure keeps the journal entry; tab/sequence metadata prevents repeating an operation already committed.

steps.title: Restore only after identity admission
steps.description: The ready snapshot identifies workspace/account, WorkspaceStorageGate admits the address, and workspaceStorage reads the correct versioned keys. Unreadable storage offers retry instead of an empty alternate store.

steps.title: Restore a send or its words
steps.description: Durable outbox records restore sends; unstored recovery records restore words only when the outbox/tombstone does not own the nonce. Missing files and sends beyond the retry window remain held for the author.

steps.title: Resume the replica without notification flood
steps.description: WebSocket hello sends lastSeq, replay is reconciled with snapshot-watermarked history, and eligible missed messages become a catch-up summary. @here replay is not treated as live presence.

flows.title: Two windows sharing local drafts and choices
flows.summary: Atomic backend merges preserve changed keys and removals. Caller-level state still needs its own reply-order ownership; Q02/Q03/Q05 record remaining gaps.

steps.title: Choose one authoritative backend
steps.description: N02 persists IndexedDB ownership before migration. Missing BroadcastChannel does not change ownership; failed opening remains unreadability with retry.

steps.title: Commit only the actual change
steps.description: A readwrite transaction merges one conversation's draft, one nonce's outbox state or one account's choice. Draft bases preserve conflicting words, and outbox tombstones/floors reject stale resurrection.

steps.title: Tell other windows
steps.description: BroadcastChannel can deliver the change; a fallback storage event carries only the changed key, then reads IndexedDB. Focus refresh and generation guards supplement that path.

steps.title: Reconcile their current views
steps.description: DraftPersistence adopts another window's drafts/outbox without overwriting its still-unsaved edits, while notification preview watchers update privacy choice. Newer local edits retain their own merge base.

steps.title: Respect the remaining caller boundaries
steps.description: Q02 requires atomic first-address registration; Q03 requires fencing old preference replies against newer watches; Q05 requires account-aware saved-signin operations. These are documented follow-ups, not claimed repairs.

flows.title: Preference-aware huddle joining and microphone recovery
flows.summary: A join has owned preference initialization, permission capture, server admission and peer media. The latest mute choice follows a replacement microphone.

steps.title: Use the shared join preference
steps.description: Header and Getting started actions wait for current initialization or saving. Unreadable preferences keep the microphone off and expose retry; a navigation guard can cancel a join no longer wanted.

steps.title: Capture before admission
steps.description: WorkspaceClient reads RTC configuration and creates HuddleSession. startLocalAudio requests the microphone and adopts it with the current mute intent; late media after cancellation is stopped.

steps.title: Join and connect peers
steps.description: Supported servers acknowledge huddle.join with a request ID; failure cleans local media. The roster chooses one offerer per peer and fixed microphone/camera/screen transceivers carry streams.

steps.title: Present audio and video once
steps.description: HuddleAudio owns remote voices; video tiles stay muted. Speaking transitions update the compact bar, while the lazy stage fits cameras and shares to the available container.

steps.title: Replace or release hardware
steps.description: After microphone loss, recovery captures the new default, applies the current mute choice and replaceTrack updates peers. Leave/destroy stops tracks, polling, device listeners and peer connections.

flows.title: App form replacement while a callback is in flight
flows.summary: A form's identity owns its input and completion. The server additionally excludes concurrent submissions of that same view, while external uncertain retries can still require app-side deduplication.

steps.title: Receive the app view
steps.description: A server ephemeral opens a ModalView in the workspace replica. ViewModal renders an AppForm keyed by that unique view ID.

steps.title: Collect form-local input
steps.description: Each block/action pair has its own value key. Busy, errors and message state belong to this keyed instance; nothing is saved to device storage.

steps.title: Submit with ownership
steps.description: An immediate submitting guard blocks a second local submit. WorkspaceClient checks the captured view ID, and Api submits the nested answer payload to the server.

steps.title: Accept only this view's result
steps.description: Success dismisses the original view ID, validation focuses its refused field, and a transport failure reports a message only while this instance remains alive.

steps.title: Keep a replacement independent
steps.description: A new view ID unmounts the old form and starts fresh state. N05 prevents the prior callback result from closing or contaminating it; N08 provides separate server-side in-flight exclusion.

flows.title: Open a workspace or message and return to the right place
flows.summary: Link parsing, account restoration, address trust and history each answer a different question: destination, credentials, local-work admission and reading position.

steps.title: Interpret the link
steps.description: Platform consumes a recognized desktop or browser fragment link. App chooses a remembered sign-in, reuses the open workspace or carries a message target through joining.

steps.title: Authenticate and identify the workspace
steps.description: JoinScreen probes compatibility and authenticates, then WorkspaceClient receives the ready snapshot. Switching destroys the previous client so no old socket/media remains active behind the new screen.

steps.title: Admit local work
steps.description: WorkspaceStorageGate checks the exact connected address for the authenticated workspace/account before mounting local-work consumers. Later aliases require approval; simultaneous first-registration remains Q02.

steps.title: Navigate and load the target
